faq.a: Personal bandwidth is your available capacity to think clearly, handle emotions, make decisions, and follow through. It’s about how much of you is available, not how many hours you have.

faq.q: What are the signs of low bandwidth?
faq.a: Common signs include struggling with simple decisions, forgetting small commitments, feeling irritated by minor things, and being busy all day without finishing much.

faq.q: How can I increase my personal bandwidth?
faq.a: Reduce drains like open loops, constant task switching, and daily decisions, and build in real recovery such as sleep, movement, and quiet breaks. Clear boundaries also protect capacity.

faq.q: Is low bandwidth the same as burnout?
faq.a: Not exactly. Low bandwidth can happen in a single day or week, while burnout is a longer-lasting state of exhaustion. If depletion lasts for weeks, it’s wise to talk with a professional.

faq.q: What does “I don’t have the bandwidth” mean?
faq.a: It’s a way of saying you don’t have the time, energy, or mental capacity to take something on right now. It borrows the tech term for how much data a connection can carry.

faq.q: Why does scrolling not feel restful?
faq.a: Scrolling keeps feeding your brain new information and small decisions, so it adds to mental load rather than lowering it. Walks, naps, and screen-free moments tend to restore more.
